cards.sentence: Gran was glad to see us at the station.
cards.why: Item vr-04-06 keys 'pleased', so sense A is 'happy about something'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: The sand was too hot to walk on without shoes.

senseB.definition: with a strong taste that burns your mouth
senseB.sentence: Dad likes his curry hot, but I like mine mild.

cards.likelierKnownNote: A child uses 'hot' for temperature from her first words, while the spicy sense comes later and mostly about food.
cards.why: vr-16-01 keys 'cold', so sense A is temperature. Spicy is a separate everyday sense (opposite mild), so the card is two-sense; 'spicy' stays a fair distractor because it is not an opposite of either sense. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: a long way up from the ground
cards.sentence: The kite was high above the trees.
cards.why: vr-16-02 keys 'low', so sense A is height above the ground. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. A 'high voice' is a stretch of the same idea, so one sense.

cards.definitionChild: before the usual or expected time
cards.sentence: We were early for the bus, so we waited at the stop.
cards.why: vr-16-03 keys 'late', so sense A is 'before the expected time'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: Tom shook the empty box, but nothing rattled.
cards.why: vr-16-04 keys 'full', so sense A is 'with nothing inside'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: My school bag felt light without all those books.

senseB.definition: bright, so you can see well
senseB.sentence: It was still light outside when we walked home.

cards.likelierKnownNote: A child uses 'light' for an easy-to-carry bag every day, while she mostly meets the bright sense as the noun, not as this adjective.
cards.why: vr-16-05 keys 'heavy', so sense A is 'not heavy'; 'bright' and 'pale' on the item belong to sense B and are not opposites of heavy. Tier 1 alongside calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to get something by paying for it
cards.sentence: We buy fresh bread from the baker on Saturdays.
cards.why: vr-16-06 keys 'sell', so sense A is 'get by paying'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: The clock hangs above the classroom door.
cards.why: vr-16-07 keys 'below', so sense A is position, a preposition. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to press against something to move it away from you
cards.sentence: Push the door hard and it will open.
cards.why: vr-16-08 keys 'pull', so sense A is 'move away by pressing'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as nudge.

cards.sentence: A rainbow began to appear over the hills.

senseB.definition: to seem, or look as if something is true
senseB.sentence: The cat appears to be asleep on the sofa.

cards.likelierKnownNote: Children use 'appear' for things coming into sight, while the 'seem' sense is mostly met in books and rarely used by them.
cards.why: vr-16-09 keys 'vanish', so sense A is 'come into view'. The distractor 'seem' belongs to sense B and is not an opposite of vanish, so the item holds. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: flat and even, with no bumps
cards.sentence: The pebble felt smooth in my hand.
cards.why: vr-16-11 keys 'rough', so sense A is texture. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as shiny, gentle.

cards.definitionChild: a long way from one side to the other
cards.sentence: The river was too wide to throw a stone across.
cards.why: vr-16-13 keys 'narrow', so sense A is distance side to side. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: The pond is deep in the middle, so stay near the edge.
cards.why: vr-16-14 keys 'shallow', so sense A is distance downward. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. A 'deep voice' or 'deep red' is treated as a stretch, not a second sense.

cards.sentence: The film will begin at six o'clock.
cards.why: Two items agree: vr-16-15 keys 'finish' (opposite) and vr-21-18 keys 'start' (same), so sense A is 'start'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to keep something in your mind and bring it back later
cards.sentence: Can you remember where you left your trainers?
cards.why: vr-16-16 keys 'forget', so sense A is 'keep in mind'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: with a fine point or an edge that can cut
cards.sentence: Mia's pencil had a sharp point after she used the sharpener.
cards.why: vr-16-17 keys 'blunt', so sense A is cutting edge or point. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. 'Sharp' for clever or sudden is treated as a stretch, so one sense.

cards.definitionChild: used to people and not wild
cards.sentence: The tame rabbit hopped onto my lap.
cards.why: vr-16-18 keys 'wild', so sense A is about animals; the 'dull' sense is rare for this age. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as gentle.

cards.definitionChild: the win at the end of a game or fight
cards.sentence: The team cheered after their victory in the final.
cards.why: vr-16-19 keys 'defeat', so sense A is winning. Tier 1 alongside brave and eager; a word children meet in sport and stories.

cards.definitionChild: to reach the place you were going to
cards.sentence: Our train will arrive at ten past nine.
cards.why: vr-16-21 keys 'depart', so sense A is reaching a place. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to get bigger and fill more space
cards.sentence: The balloon will expand as you blow into it.
cards.why: vr-16-22 keys 'shrink', so sense A is 'get bigger'. Tier 2 beside fragile and ancient: understood, but a school word children rarely use in speech.

cards.sentence: We watched the hot air balloon rise into the sky.
cards.why: vr-16-23 keys 'fall', so sense A is 'go up'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: Her face lit up with joy when she saw the puppy.
cards.why: vr-16-24 keys 'sorrow', so sense A is great happiness. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to take something that is offered to you
cards.sentence: Mum said I could accept the invitation to the party.
cards.why: vr-16-25 keys 'refuse', so sense A is 'take what is offered'. Tier 1 alongside fetch and mend, though borderline with tier 2.

cards.sentence: The giant had broad shoulders and a big laugh.
cards.why: vr-21-01 keys 'wide', so sense A is width. Tier 1 alongside brisk and swift, which sit at the same reading level; borderline with tier 2.

cards.sentence: The cake was soft and moist inside.
cards.why: vr-21-02 keys 'damp', so sense A is slightly wet. Tier 1 alongside damp, its own key and a tier 1 exemplar.

cards.sentence: It was foolish to leave the picnic out in the rain.
cards.why: vr-21-03 keys 'silly', so sense A is 'not sensible'. Tier 1 alongside eager and curious; a fairy-tale word children know well.

cards.sentence: The frog will leap from one lily pad to the next.
cards.why: vr-21-04 keys 'jump', so sense A is the verb. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as dart.

cards.definitionChild: to take hold of something quickly
cards.sentence: Grab the rope with both hands!
cards.why: vr-21-05 keys 'seize', so sense A is 'take hold quickly'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as grip.

cards.definitionChild: to come to the end of something
cards.sentence: I want to finish my book before bedtime.
cards.why: vr-21-06 keys 'end', so sense A is the verb 'come to the end'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to make something by putting parts together
cards.sentence: We will build a sandcastle by the sea.
cards.why: vr-21-07 keys 'construct', so sense A is 'make by putting parts together'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: having lived for a long time
cards.sentence: The old lady next door can remember life eighty years ago.

senseB.definition: not new, and used for a long time
senseB.sentence: We found a rusty old bike at the back of the shed.

cards.likelierKnownNote: A child uses the age sense herself whenever she calls a grandparent, a neighbour or a pet old, more readily than she calls a thing old for not being new.
cards.why: vr-21-08 keys 'elderly', which fits people only, so sense A is a person's age (opposite young). 'Not new' (opposite new) is a separate everyday sense, so the card is two-sense. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: The rich king lived in a palace full of gold.
cards.why: vr-21-09 keys 'wealthy', so sense A is money. 'Rich food' is treated as a stretch, so one sense. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: After the long walk, the children were tired and hungry.
cards.why: vr-21-11 keys 'weary' (a tier 3 exemplar), so sense A is needing rest. Tier 1 alongside calm; the headword is far easier than its key.

cards.sentence: The puppy looked happy when we came home.
cards.why: vr-21-12 keys 'glad', so sense A is cheerful. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to make a job easier for someone
cards.sentence: Can you help me carry the shopping inside?
cards.why: vr-21-13 keys 'assist', so sense A is the verb. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to pick one thing from a group
cards.sentence: You can choose any book from the shelf.
cards.why: vr-21-14 keys 'select', so sense A is 'pick'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: strange or not what you expect
cards.sentence: There was an odd smell coming from the fridge.

senseB.definition: a number that cannot be split into two equal whole numbers
senseB.sentence: Seven is an odd number, but eight is not.

cards.likelierKnownNote: Children are taught odd and even numbers from their first years at school and use that sense with care, more surely than 'odd' for strange.
cards.why: vr-21-15 keys 'strange', so sense A is strange. The distractor 'even' is the opposite in sense B, not a synonym, so the item holds. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: I wrapped a gift for my best friend's birthday.
cards.why: vr-21-16 keys 'present', so sense A is a thing given. 'A gift for music' is treated as a stretch, so one sense. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: Please speak clearly so everyone can hear you.
cards.why: vr-21-17 keys 'talk', so sense A is saying words. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.definitionChild: to move something so it is no longer open
cards.sentence: Please shut the gate so the dog stays in.
cards.why: vr-21-19 keys 'close', so sense A is the verb. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: We saw a big ship sailing into the harbour.
cards.why: vr-21-20 keys 'large', so sense A is size. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: Sam was quick to put his hand up.
cards.why: vr-21-21 keys 'rapid', so sense A is speed. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as swift.

cards.sentence: The kitten was scared of the noisy vacuum cleaner.
cards.why: vr-21-22 keys 'fearful', so sense A is feeling afraid. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: Dad was angry when the dog chewed his slipper.
cards.why: vr-21-23 keys 'cross', so sense A is the feeling. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.

cards.sentence: The library was silent while everyone read.
cards.why: vr-21-24 keys 'quiet', so sense A is 'making no sound'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy. Same floor as noisy.

cards.definitionChild: not hard to do or understand
cards.sentence: The recipe was simple enough for me to make alone.
cards.why: vr-21-25 keys 'easy', so sense A is 'not hard'. Tier 1 alongside everyday exemplars brave, calm, huge, tidy.
